key_insight: OpenEarthAgent provides a unified framework that augments multimodal agents with geospatial tools and satellite-trained capabilities so they can reason coherently across spatial scales, spectral bands, and multi-step analytical workflows.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between generic multimodal reasoning and remote sensing needs by enabling agents to handle geographic scale, structured geospatial logic, and multispectral indices within tool-assisted, multi-step analyses.
method: Design a tool-augmented agent architecture that integrates geospatial utilities (e.g., GIS queries, spectral-index calculators, map/tiling services) with an LLM-style planner.
Train and fine-tune multimodal models on satellite imagery + geospatial metadata to align visual, spectral, and textual reasoning for remote sensing tasks.
Use modular, interpretable tool invocation and stepwise reasoning to perform structured tasks (e.g., change detection, land-cover mapping, index computation) across scales.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to build robust, extensible geospatial agents that automate complex Earth-observation analyses and integrate domain tools, accelerating deployment of applied remote sensing workflows.
visual_elements: High-level architecture diagram showing LLM planner, tool set (GIS, index calculators, databases), and satellite imagery inputs
Before/after map overlays (e.g., change detection or land-cover classification) to illustrate outputs
Tool invocation flowchart showing a multi-step query → tool call → result → next-step loop
Compact performance/use-case summary (icons + short metrics) comparing tasks like detection, mapping, and index retrieval
paper_title: OpenEarthAgent: A Unified Framework for Tool-Augmented Geospatial Agents
paper_authors: Akashah Shabbir, Muhammad Umer Sheikh, Muhammad Akhtar Munir, Hiyam Debary, Mustansar Fiaz
